title: CH27: no /approve, /deny, /reply or /answer — a blocked session cannot be resolved from the command bar
repro: Fleet: kestrel at its permission prompt, beacon at its AskUserQuestion
Open Home; type `/approve kestrel` ⏎, `/deny kestrel` ⏎, `/reply beacon Postgres` ⏎, `/answer beacon 2` ⏎
Type `/` and read the hint list
expected: Approve / deny / answer / reply resolve from the bar in ≤ 2 keys (e.g. `/approve kestrel`), with the same exact-tab safety as the row buttons, and say whether the keystroke landed.
actual: "Unknown command /approve. Type / to see them." (same for /deny, /reply, /answer). The 8 listed commands include nothing that answers a session; the only session action is `/jump`, which fails on tmux.
truth: kestrel waiting(permission prompt) 228 s; beacon waiting(input needed) 227 s (01:58:28Z)

title: CH27/CH28/CH29: chat cannot reach any session: '@kestrel approve' and 'tell the vibepet session to run its tests' only go to the model; /reply and /approve are unknown; no [Send to session] or permission card
repro: Lease kestrel (at its permission prompt); type '@kestrel approve', Enter; check kestrel's transcript, registry and pane
Lease vibepet (idle); type 'tell the vibepet session to run its tests', Enter; check its transcript
expected: the approval reaches kestrel (deploy.sh runs); vibepet gets the prompt and runs its tests; each result is shown in chat
actual: replies: 'I can't send approvals to agents…' / 'I can't send commands to agents…'. kestrel: transcript still 252 lines, registry still waiting, pane still 'Do you want to proceed?'. vibepet: still 128 lines, idle. '/reply' and '/approve' → 'Unknown command'. Replies carry only a 'copy' button, never [Send to session]
truth: kestrel waiting / permission prompt for ./deploy.sh --dry-run (569 s at 02:13:18Z); vibepet idle 13 min (02:08:00Z)

title: CH22/B5.1: '@' in the composer opens nothing (no session, file, port or diff picker)
expected: a fuzzy, keyboard-driven picker of live sessions, files, ports and 'diff'
actual: '@' stays plain text; no picker element exists

title: Ambiguous names resolve silently to one session: `/jump a` → vibepet (3 matches), `/replay run` → atlas; the tie-break follows a clock that restarts every tick (M4)
repro: Rows: vibepet "Read package.json" (ready), ember (ready), beacon "Beacon database choice", kestrel "Deploy.sh dry run", atlas "Run build.sh" (running)
Type `/jump run` ⏎ nine times over 40 s; type `/replay run` ⏎
expected: With several matches the bar lists them (or asks which), and never acts on a pick the user cannot predict.
actual: `e` (4 matches) and `a` (3 matches: vibepet, beacon, atlas) both jumped to vibepet with no mention of the others; `/replay a` opened "Theater — vibepet". "run" matches kestrel and atlas: at 01:55:15Z the bar's matcher ranked kestrel first, from 01:55:38Z all 9 real runs went to atlas — its row clock restarts every few seconds ("atlas · 0s"), making it the newest. `/replay run` opened "Theater — atlas".
truth: kestrel waiting(permission prompt) 35–97 s and beacon waiting(input needed) 35–97 s (both shown as running); atlas busy (build.sh) 82–147 s; vibepet idle (done) 13–35 s

title: /goal cannot name its session: `/goal kestrel: approve the deploy` set ember's goal to "kestrel: approve the deploy"
repro: Only ember is shown in Home (kestrel live but hidden)
expected: `/goal <session> <text>` (or an @session) targets the named session; an unmatched name is refused, not applied to another session.
actual: "Goal for ember: kestrel: approve the deploy"; ember's row shows ◎ kestrel: approve the deploy (set-goal reached main with ember's id at 4 ms). The target is always the ◎-picked row, else the top row.
truth: kestrel waiting(permission prompt) 4795 s; ember idle (loop) 264 s (01:52:48Z)

title: /replay <name> searches only Home's live list: 'No session matches “kestrel”' for all six members while ⋯ → Theater… lists all of them
repro: Type '/replay kestrel' and Enter; repeat with beacon, vibepet, atlas, delta, ember
expected: Each opens that session's replay (all six transcripts exist and Theater… lists them)
actual: Six notes 'No session matches “<name>”.'; no window. A minute later Theater… listed 8 sessions including all six
truth: kestrel approval, beacon question, vibepet done, atlas idle, delta and ember exited (01:43:41Z); transcripts present for all

title: CH33/CH22: the hint list is not keyboard-driven and has no argument completion — ↑/↓ do nothing, Tab goes to Send, ⏎ on a unique prefix fails, no session/port/@ picker
expected: ↑/↓ move through hints, Tab/⏎ complete; a unique prefix completes or runs; after `/jump ` or `/replay ` a picker of live sessions (or ports for /stop) appears; `@` mentions sessions.
actual: ↓ ↓ ⏎ → "Unknown command /."; `/tod` ⏎ → "Unknown command /tod."; Tab focuses the Send button and only a 2nd Tab reaches the first hint; `@` opens nothing and the hint list hides as soon as a space is typed.

title: CH33/B7.3: the slash menu is mouse-only: ↓ selects nothing, Tab jumps to Send, Esc closes the whole panel and leaves '/' behind
repro: Press ↓, then Tab; click back into the composer and press Esc
expected: ↑↓ move a selection, Tab/Enter complete, Esc dismisses only the menu
actual: no item is selected on ↓; Tab focuses the Send button; Esc hides the panel with '/' still in the composer

title: Esc with the hint list open closes the whole Home panel instead of the list
expected: First Esc dismisses the hint list; a second Esc closes the panel.
actual: Panel hidden in 0.3 ms; reopening keeps the draft `/rep` with its hint.

title: CH33 on Theater: /replay can't be completed from the keyboard: Tab after '/rep' moves focus to Send, ↓ does nothing, no session-name suggestions
expected: Tab completes '/replay ' and suggests session names; ↑↓ pick
actual: Input stays '/rep'; focus jumps to the Send button; ↓ no effect

title: A failed command clears the bar, so a typo must be retyped from scratch
expected: The text stays (selected) so it can be fixed.
actual: The bar is empty after every no-match and unknown-command note.

title: Edge-case copy: `/stop` → "Nothing listening on ."; `/` → "Unknown command /. Type / to see them."; `/Today` is unknown (commands are case-sensitive)
expected: "/stop needs a port, e.g. /stop 3000"; "/" alone opens the list; commands match case-insensitively.
